speaker: Doctor
text: Dr. Agent: I see a painful, ulcerative lesion on your leg. To narrow this down, have you noticed any recent insect bites, trauma, or a travel history to areas with endemic diseases?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the history. Given your history of Crohn's disease and diabetes, along with the ant bite and lesion progression, have you noticed any systemic symptoms like fever, night sweats, or significant weight loss recently? Also, is the ulcer currently draining any fluid?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
REQUEST TEST: Complete Blood Count (CBC) with differential and Erythrocyte Sedimentation Rate (ESR).

Please confirm if you have experienced any recent fevers or chills, and describe the appearance of the pitting edema and the tortuous veins in more detail.
